title: Remove 'that' from the neutral words
defect: 'move A left, after that move B up' was accepted with the order REVERSED (B first): a comma does not close the row, so 'after' acted as the infix connector 'A after B'. The word 'that' was a neutral (zero-vector) token, so the network could not tell 'after that' from 'after'. Found by the hand-written adversarial suite (tests/next/adversarial.jsonl), not by the generated benchmark.
hypothesis: 'after that' is not part of the documented grammar. If 'that' is not a lexicon word it embeds as the unknown-token vector, err_unknown_token fires, and every construction containing 'that' is rejected instead of being silently mis-ordered.
affected: lexicon (neutral word 'that' removed): embedding row E['that'] is no longer a zero row; the token falls back to the <unk> row.
mathematical_effect: x_UNK = 1 for the token, so the error detector unit err_unknown_token = relu(x_UNK) adds 1 to the sticky error mass, which exceeds the reject threshold 0.5.
expected: tests/next/defects-003.jsonl: all 150 rejected (was: all accepted). No change on the dev set and earlier defect suites.
